scenario.name: Halcyon, AWS Security & MITRE — AWS S3 Server-Side KMS External Key (SSE-KMS) Re-Encryption Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a cloud-native ransomware crew that never drops a single piece of malware on any computer. Instead, using stolen cloud warehouse keys, they bring their own external padlock from an outside account, use the warehouse own built-in copier to re-seal every customer box in place under their external padlock, and set the warehouse automatic trash chute to one day so all previous unlocked editions are swept away before the ransom note arrives. In this scenario (T1619, Halcyon, AWS Security & MITRE, AWS S3 Server-Side KMS External Key , SSE-KMS Re-Encryption Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: cross-Account KMS Key Policy Grant, then in-Place S3 CopyObject Re-Encryption, then putBucketLifecycleConfiguration 1-Day. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Cross-Account KMS Key Policy Grant, then In-Place S3 CopyObject Re-Encryption, then PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration 1-Day, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Enforce an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) with Condition StringNotEquals aws:ResourceAccount / s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id to forbid encrypting S3 objects with KMS keys outside the organization.

stages.title: Stage 1: Cross-Account KMS Key Policy Grant & S3 Bucket Inventory Enumeration
stages.subtitle: Resource Development & Discovery (T1619 - Cloud Storage Object Discovery)
stages.description: Inside their own separate cloud account, the extortionist forges a brand-new encryption padlock and authorizes the victim cloud badge to lock boxes with it, while quietly mapping every valuable storage bucket inside the victim estate. Using compromised IAM credentials with s3:ListBucket and s3:PutObject permissions, the actor configures a KMS Customer Managed Key (CMK) in an external AWS account that permits kms:Encrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey* from the victim account (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventSource=s3.amazonaws.com, TargetBucket=prod-enterprise-records, ActorPrincipal=backup-sync-svc so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=ListBuckets (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=ListBu so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1619 during "Cross-Account KMS Key Policy Grant & S3 Bucket Inventory Enumeration" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket prod-enterprise-records runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket prod-enterprise-records against AWS CloudTrail, GCP so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1619 during "Cross-Account KMS Key Policy Grant & S3 Bucket Inventory Enumeration" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ ListObjectsV2 on bucket prod-enterprise-records / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 External AWS Account KMS CMK) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 S3 Object Versioning & Lifecycle Policy).

stages.title: Stage 2: In-Place S3 CopyObject Re-Encryption with External Account SSE-KMS Key ARN
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact)
stages.description: Issuing rapid in-place copy orders straight through the cloud storage service itself, the extortionist forces the warehouse to overwrite every file with a fresh copy sealed strictly under the attacker external padlock, instantly locking the rightful owner out once the attacker revokes access to their external key. Without downloading or re-uploading the data, the actor invokes s3:CopyObject (copying each object onto itself) with x-amz-server-side-encryption="aws:kms" and x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id pointing to arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:999988887777:key/<external_cmk_id>, logged in S3 Data Events (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventName=CopyObject , In-Place Server-Side Re-Encryption, EncryptionMode=aws:kms , SSE-KMS, ExternalKmsKeyArn=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:999988887777:key/44556677-8899-aabb-ccdd-eeff00112233 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '.Records[] | select(.eventName=="CopyObject" and .requestParameters."x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id" | contains, "999988887777")' s3_data_events.json (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '.Records[] | select.eventName=="CopyObject" and .requestParameters."x-amz-server-sid so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1486 during "In-Place S3 CopyObject Re-Encryption with External Account SSE-KMS Key ARN" , Without downloading or re-uploading the data, the actor invokes s3:CopyObject , copying each object onto itself with x-amz-server-side-encryption="aws:kms" and x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id pointing to arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:999988887777:key/<external_cmk_id>, logged in S3 Data Events while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact aws s3api head-object --bucket prod-enterprise-records --key financial-ledger-2026.parquet runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws s3api head-object --bucket prod-enterprise-records --key financial-ledger-2026.parquet ag so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1486 during "In-Place S3 CopyObject Re-Encryption with External Account SSE-KMS Key ARN" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ CopyObject in-place with external SSE-KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:999988887777:key/ext-cmk / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 AWS S3 API (CopyObject SSE-KMS)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 S3 Object Versioning & Lifecycle Policy).

keySpecs.value: Attach an S3 Bucket Policy denying s3:PutObject and s3:CopyObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id does not match the organization approved KMS key ARN.

stages.title: Stage 3: PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration 1-Day NoncurrentVersionExpiration & Object Lock Recovery
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1490 - Inhibit System Recovery)
stages.description: Even if the warehouse keeps older unlocked versions of every box on a safety shelf, the extortionist silently adjusts the warehouse automated housekeeping rule to incinerate all non-current versions after a single day unless Object Lock bolts the shelf shut. To purge prior unencrypted object versions on versioned buckets, the actor calls s3:PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration with NoncurrentVersionExpiration set to 1 day. Defenders block deletion by removing the malicious lifecycle rule and restoring prior S3 VersionIds protected by S3 Object Lock (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventName=PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration, LifecycleRuleAction=NoncurrentVersionExpiration , NoncurrentDays: 1, RecoveryPivot=DeleteLifecycle + Restore prior S3 VersionId so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes aws s3api delete-bucket-lifecycle --bucket prod-enterprise-records (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws s3api delete-bucket-lifecycle --bucket prod-enterprise-records against AWS CloudTrail, GC so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1490 during "PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration 1-Day NoncurrentVersionExpiration & Object Lock Recovery" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket prod-enterprise-records --prefix financial-ledger-2026.parquet runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket prod-enterprise-records --prefix financial-ledger-202 so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1490 during "PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration 1-Day NoncurrentVersionExpiration & Object Lock Recovery" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration (NoncurrentVersionExpiration NoncurrentDays=1) / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 AWS S3 API (CopyObject SSE-KMS)) to Node ④ (#4 Production S3 Bucket Objects), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 S3 Object Versioning & Lifecycle Policy).

keySpecs.value: Enable S3 Versioning with MFA Delete and S3 Object Lock (Compliance or Governance mode), and alert immediately on PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration events in CloudTrail.
